trust_decision.summary: An authenticated user may make the server fetch any URL: the published fix decides that only http/https URLs which resolve to a public address may be fetched, and enforces that at every fetch site in the scraper services and the form image transformer via a new ScrapingUrlGuard, plus NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient and a Chrome host-resolver pin for the Panther path.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'authenticated SSRF' in the scraper, so the first place an engineer looks is the HTML scraper's navigation to $scraping->getUrl(); the sibling sinks at src/Service/Scraper/HtmlScraper.php:73 and src/Service/Scraper/JsonScraper.php:42 are one screen away, while the form transformer and the collection-scraper image fetch are not.

fix_sites.module_kind: service (abstract HTML scraper base class; curl fallback and headless-Chrome path)

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /scrapers/item-scrapers/scrap, POST /scrapers/wish-scrapers/scrap, POST /scrapers/collection-scrapers/scrap (scraper content type json)
fix_sites.module_kind: service (abstract JSON scraper base class, injectable HTTP client)

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /items/add, POST /items/{id}/edit, POST /wishes/add, POST /wishes/{id}/edit, POST /collections/add, POST /collections/{id}/edit (hidden fileUrl / fileImageUrl fields)
fix_sites.module_kind: form data transformer (form layer, separate package from the scraper services)

fix_sites.entry_point: n/a - new shared guard service called from the three sites above

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about the scraper feature, so a solver can argue the image transformer is a form-layer path whose value is a hidden field filled by the scraper's own JavaScript, and the collection image URL is read out of the scraped page rather than supplied by the user.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Protocol-relative image URLs ('//cdn.example.com/x.jpg') must still be fetched - the transformer rewrites them to https: before any check, so a guard placed before the rewrite rejects them; likewise scraping a locally uploaded file (a real File in the 'file' field, src/Service/Scraper/HtmlScraper.php:19-21 and src/Service/Scraper/JsonScraper.php:31-32) must keep working with no URL at all, so a guard at the top of scrap() breaks file-based scraping.

O6_input_shapes: uppercase scheme (HTTPS://) - lowercased before the allowlist test
protocol-relative //host/path, rewritten to https: by the transformer before the guard sees it
non-http schemes file://, file:/, FILE://, gopher://, ftp://, data:, about:blank
IPv4 literal host and bracketed IPv6 literal host ('[::1]', brackets trimmed)
hostname needing DNS resolution, both A and AAAA records
uploaded File instead of a URL (guard is skipped by design)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The collection scraper fetches a second, attacker-influenced URL - the image path extracted from the scraped document and re-based by guessHost - with the injected client directly, and the published fix never puts the guard on that call; a solver who adds assertSchemeIsSupported/resolvePublicAddress only inside getCrawler leaves it open.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The image URL is taken from the scraped page, not from the user, and the injected client is already the one the main fix wrapped in NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient, so it looks covered.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package but a different class from the fixed base class: subclass 2 files away from JsonScraper, entered through the /scrapers/collection-scrapers/scrap route

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Fetch the scraped image through a client held on the HTML scraper, i.e. the same image-download sink as the JSON twin
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The line already performs exactly this fetch against an undefined $this->client (a latent bug at the pinned commit) and the published fix adds a constructor to HtmlScraper without adding a client, so the next maintainer to repair this class completes the sink and can easily omit the guard.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second /tmp-writing image transformer in the same directory that keeps its own bare new CurlHttpClient() with neither the guard nor NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The neighbouring transformer already constructs a bare CurlHttpClient in its constructor and is wired into the album, collection, wishlist and profile forms; a URL-fed variant of it (or a cache/preview fetch added to it) copies that shape exactly.

O9_family: server-side request forgery (CWE-918): unfiltered outbound HTTP request to a URL supplied or influenced by an authenticated user

O10_build.toolchain: PHP >= 8.5 with composer (composer.json:10), Symfony 8.1 (symfony/http-client 8.1.3), yarn/webpack for assets, PHPUnit 13 + paratest + Zenstruck Foundry, Dockerfile and CI workflow present
services: MySQL/MariaDB/PostgreSQL database for the functional tests
O10_build.project_tests: tests/App/Scraper/{Item,Wish,Collection}ScraperTest.php cover only the scraper CRUD/index/export/import routes and never trigger a fetch; no test at the pinned commit exercises the scraping or image-URL paths (the fix adds tests/App/Scraper/ScrapingUrlGuardTest.php, absent from the pinned tree).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Validate only the scraper URL inside HtmlScraper::fetchWithPanther (or at the top of each scrap()), treating the page the user asked to scrape as the only untrusted input.

out_of_scope_notes: Nothing outside this advisory's protection was pursued; the only other outbound request in the tree, src/Service/LatestReleaseChecker.php:43, targets a hard-coded GitHub URL and is not user-controlled, so it is not a route to this sink.
